title: The Three Days of Life and the Two Deaths: The Whole Arc of Redemption and Its Opposite
arc: The teaching lays out the entire spiritual drama as three Great Days (descent-and-mingling, intermediate reign in the new aeon, and final unveiling of the Father in eternal conjunction) set against two Deaths (the temporal death of light-mingled-in-darkness which ends with purification, and the eternal second death of those who have permanently severed themselves from the Lord by blaspheming the Holy Spirit).
reading:
This chapter answers a single question: what is the complete shape of spiritual time? The master gives the answer in two matched series — three Great Days that name the full motion of life from God toward God, and two Deaths that name what stands opposite that motion. Read together, they are the whole correspondential geography of redemption.

The **First Day** is the era of descent and mingling. It begins when the First Man — Divine Truth in its descent into the natural — goes down into the Deep of Darkness and "receives submergence" there. This is the Lord's accommodation into the realm of self-love so that the captive light may be reached. The Living Spirit then brings him up; he ascends to the Father of Life and rules over the works above and below. Within this same Day the Third Ambassador comes to be seated in the ship of the Day and reveals his glorious image, refining out (purifying) what can be drawn out of the mingled state, and then walks in the heights until the cosmos is finally released. So the First Day is not a single moment but the whole epoch of the cosmos as we now know it: the era in which the First Man with his Five Sons (the five-fold Living Soul, Divine Truth in five-fold completeness) is mingled with the Darkness, and in which the Lord through descent, raising, and revealing image works to extract the light. The "three matters" done in this first Day — descent, raising, and revealing — are the inner pattern of all redemption.

The **Second Day** is the era of the new aeon, when the Fathers of Light who reigned in the original aeon shall sit upon thrones in the new aeon, dwell in the new land, and reign in the new tabernacle. This corresponds to the established heavenly state after the cosmos has done its purifying work: the redeemed seated upon their thrones of dominion, each in his own measure proportioned to the first Day, each in his own aeon and tabernacle. It is the state of stable conjunction — but conjunction not yet consummated, because the Father has not yet unveiled his innermost image.

The **Third Day** is the consummation. Now the Father himself reveals forth his image upon them, conveys them upward into his hidden ones — the storehouses, the inmost degrees of stored divine good. They behold the ambrosia and the sweet fragrance (the diffusing presence of divine love), and looking upon her their eyes are filled with breadth and joy unto eternity. Their hearts are made new. From that hour onward they are no longer counted by the number of days and hours, no longer reckoned by time at all; they have entered the state where the Father will never again hide his face. The Third Day is therefore not another era within history but the breaking-in of the eternal: the unveiling of the Father's inmost, the perfecting of all aeons in one measure, the immeasurable richness that lies beyond all counting.

The three Days together describe the complete arc of spiritual life as the doctrine of correspondences sees it: descent of Divine Truth into the natural for the sake of mingled light, the establishment of the new state in the aeon (the regenerate condition formed and stabilized), and the final celestial unveiling in which the soul is gathered into the Father's hidden storehouses and conjunction becomes eternal. They are the three discrete degrees of the saving process — natural (descent and refining), spiritual (reign in the new aeon), celestial (the Father's image revealed without veil).

Against this triple Day stand the **two Deaths**. The first Death is the cosmos itself considered as the state of severance: it begins when the Light fell into the Darkness and was mingled with it, and it lasts until the Light is purified and separated forth from the Darkness in the great fire. This is "death" in the correspondential sense — life held in non-conjunction, the Living Soul crucified in matter — but it is a death that ends. What remains after the purifying fire is built up and added to the last Panaretos, the consummating image of redeemed light (the Last Andrias). So the first Death is the very condition the three Days are working through; it is for-a-season.

The second Death is altogether different. It is the death the sinners die: separation from the Light, from the glory that sheds light upon the cosmos, from the living Air (the breath of spiritual perception), from being nourished any longer by the living Soul in the cosmos. They are separated forth and driven away from the last Panaretos itself — that is, they cannot be gathered into the final image of redeemed light. They are bound, given over to torment and affliction in the three places of judgment, because they blasphemed the Holy Spirit through generations of the cosmos. This is the final clod, the bolos, the residue that cannot be refined, fixed in the eternal state of self-love. The first Death lasts for a season; the second is forever.

The teaching's whole power lies in this symmetry. Time itself, in the spiritual sense, has only two ultimate trajectories. Either the soul moves through the three Days — accepting the descent of the First Man, being raised by the Living Spirit, illumined by the Ambassador's revealed image, established upon a throne in the new aeon, and finally drawn into the Father's hidden storehouses where counting ceases — or it remains in the first Death and, by blaspheming the operative Spirit that alone can refine it, hardens into the second Death where separation becomes permanent. The Days are the count of redemption; the Deaths are what falls outside the count. And the eternal Third Day and the eternal second Death are the two final unchangeable states toward which everything in the cosmos is now tending.
